final_codebook.domain: Subtracting fractions and mixed numbers, including preparatory rewriting, direct subtraction, regrouping, and final simplification

skills.name: Rewrite into compatible form
skills.definition: Rewrite one or both quantities into equivalent subtraction-ready forms before subtracting, including finding common denominators, converting equivalent fractions, normalizing mixed numbers with improper fractional parts, simplifying a fractional part before subtraction, or writing a whole number with a fractional part.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the step finds an LCD/common denominator and converts fractions to equivalent fractions.
Tag when the step rewrites a mixed number with an improper or nonstandard fractional part into a standard mixed number.
Tag when the step simplifies a fractional part before subtraction so the numbers are easier to align.
Tag when the step rewrites a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator or otherwise rewrites quantities so fractional parts are compatible.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag the actual subtraction once the quantities are already compatible.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping after subtraction reveals the fractional part is too small.
Do not tag final simplification or final answer formatting after subtraction unless the rewrite is clearly preparatory.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Carry out subtraction once the quantities are in compatible form, including subtracting like fractions and subtracting whole and fractional parts of mixed numbers when no regrouping is performed in that step.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted over a shared denominator.
Tag when whole parts and fractional parts of mixed numbers are subtracted directly after alignment.
Tag when a step performs subtraction that may produce an intermediate negative fractional difference before a later regrouping step.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag steps whose main purpose is creating common denominators or otherwise rewriting forms before subtraction.
Do not tag the borrowing/regrouping step itself.
Do not tag simplification-only or final-expression-only steps when no subtraction is performed.

skills.name: Borrow across whole
skills.definition: Regroup by taking 1 from the whole-number part and converting it into fractional units so subtraction can continue when the fractional part of the minuend is too small.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the step explicitly borrows 1 from the whole-number part.
Tag when the borrowed whole is converted into denominator-sized fractional units and added to the existing fractional part.
Tag when regrouping resolves a negative or insufficient fractional difference in a mixed-number or whole-minus-fraction subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag ordinary subtraction steps that do not regroup.
Do not tag merely rewriting a whole number as having 0 fractional units before any borrowing occurs.
Do not tag final simplification or combining after regrouping is complete.

skills.name: Simplify and express result
skills.definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms and express it appropriately as a fraction, mixed number, integer, or zero by combining or removing parts as needed.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a fraction is simplified after subtraction, such as 9/12 to 3/4 or 0/3 to 0.
Tag when whole and fractional parts are combined into a mixed number or integer final answer.
Tag when a zero whole part or zero fractional part is removed to express the final result appropriately.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag preparatory rewrites done before subtraction.
Do not tag subtraction computation itself.

decisions.reasoning: C01 had 3/3 consensus and C02 had only 1/3 consensus, but dossier evidence shows normalization of improper mixed numbers is a subtype of the broader preparatory rewriting process rather than an independently necessary skill in this item set. Keeping them separate would reduce minimality and create boundary ambiguity, since experts A and B already embedded normalization inside rewriting. Merging preserves completeness while improving clarity and identifiability.

decisions.details: Refined C01 into S01 'Rewrite into compatible form'
decisions.reasoning: The definition was broadened slightly to explicitly include all preparatory equivalent-form operations evidenced across experts and dossiers: common denominators, equivalent fractions, normalization of improper mixed-number parts, simplification before subtraction, and rewriting whole numbers with fractional parts. This yields clearer annotation boundaries.

This skill had 3/3 consensus and is independently testable from rewriting, borrowing, and simplification. Items such as FS06 require direct subtraction without any rewriting or regrouping, confirming strong diagnostic value.

Although only 2/3 consensus, borrowing/regrouping is a distinct cognitive operation with clear dossier evidence in items such as FS07, FS10, FS13, FS15, FS17, FS18, FS19, and FS20. It is independently testable and should remain separate from both subtraction and simplification under the non-redundancy principle.

This skill had 3/3 consensus and is distinct from both subtraction and borrowing. Dossiers include simplification-only and expression-only steps, such as converting 0/3 to 0 or combining parts into a mixed number, so it supports diagnostic resolution.

decisions.details: Removed standalone candidate C02 after merging into S01
decisions.reasoning: As a separate skill, normalization of mixed numbers was too narrow and not consistently distinguished by experts. It did not satisfy minimality well enough to justify one of the four available slots once a broader rewrite skill was retained.

summary: The final codebook preserves the shared four-stage workflow supported by the strongest cross-expert consensus and the dossier evidence: preparatory rewriting, direct subtraction, borrowing/regrouping, and simplification/final expression. The main consolidation decision was to absorb the low-consensus 'Normalize mixed numbers' candidate into the broader rewrite skill, because it functions as a subtype of equivalent-form preparation rather than a reliably separate diagnosable skill in this item set.
